subject: SAML attribute release: justification, entropy analysis & SCIM provisioning logs
messages:
From: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@finserv.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: security_assurance@finserv.com
Date: 2026-06-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: SAML attribute release: justification + logs needed

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG intake for Redwood (deadline: 2026-06-25), our security team needs the following artifacts to complete the attribute-release / provisioning section:  

- A short justification for every attribute you release in the SAML assertion (name, email, username, groups, department, custom attributes). We need to know why each attribute is required by the service and an explanation of minimality/least-privilege.
- A sample SAML assertion (redacted) showing attribute names/values (ideally 2 examples: new user, returned user).
- SCIM provisioning delta logs for the last 30 days (create/update/delete events) and a short note about how user lifecycle events map to internal roles.
- Role activation logs that show how elevated roles are granted and who approved them (audit trail).

Can you confirm you can provide these by EOD 2026-06-18? Also, do you have an entropy/uniqueness assessment for attributes that might be PII (we need to assess re-identification risk)?

Appreciate it — we’ll bundle this into our SIG response.

Best,
Alice Bennett
Senior Security Assurance Manager
FinServ Holdings

[On Mon, Jun 14, 2026 at 08:45 Sofia asked about the scope before this thread — included here for context]
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@finserv.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SAML attribute release: justification + logs needed

Hi Alice,

Thanks — we can take this. Quick summary of plan and a couple clarifying Qs:  

Plan (deliverables by 2026-06-18 EOD):
- saml-attribute-samples.csv (two redacted assertions: new user, returning user) — includes attribute name, purpose, minimal justification.
- scim-delta-20260530-0606.zip — exported delta events (create/update/delete) for the last 30 days; CSV manifest included.
- role-activation-logs-2026-05.txt — scrubbed activation/approval trace for elevated roles.
- short note on attribute entropy and re-identification risk for attributes we consider sensitive.

Clarifying Qs:
1) For the entropy assessment, do you want absolute metrics (Shannon entropy per attribute) or a qualitative risk statement? We can include both but the absolute numbers are noisy unless you want the raw frequency tables.
2) Any constraints on sample assertions (e.g., must include full NameID format, or are transient NameIDs okay)?

Cc’ing Marcus and Karthik — Marcus will attach the role activation export and Karthik will help with the SCIM delta extraction. Priya will review for redaction.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Security & Compliance (Redwood Inference)
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

On Mon, Jun 14, 2026 at 09:12 Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@finserv.com> wrote:  
> (original request)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@finserv.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-16T14:21:00Z
Subject: Re: SAML attribute release: justification + logs needed

Sofia — attaching role activation export and brief notes.

Attachment stubs:
- role-activation-logs-2026-05.txt (contains: timestamp, actor, target-role, approval-id, justification snippet where available)
- runbook-link: https://redwood-inference.internal/runbooks/role-approval (internal)

Notes (summary):
- Elevated roles (ops: deploy-admin, infra:gpu-admin) require a two-step approval: ticket creation in Jira -> manager approval in the console. Approval IDs are correlated to Jira ticket IDs.
- Activation windows are time-limited (default 8 hours) and are automatically revoked.
- We redacted email addresses except for linkage via approval-id; full audit available under eDiscovery for audits.

Also: I pulled the owner mapping for groups -> roles; that is in the saml-attribute-samples.csv under the 'groups_usage' column. Priya will sanity-check the redactions.

—Marcus
Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jun 16, 2026 at 11:05 Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai> wrote:  
> (Sofia’s plan)
From: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@finserv.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: security_assurance@finserv.com
Date: 2026-06-18T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: SAML attribute release: justification + logs needed

Thanks — this looks good and on the face of it should satisfy the SIG reviewers. Two small follow-ups before we close the intake:  

1) Could you include a single-row user snapshot (redacted) showing attribute cardinality for the most common attributes (email, username, groups) so we can see how many unique values and sample frequencies? That will help our re-identification risk model.

2) For the groups -> role mapping, can you confirm whether group names are stable identifiers (we prefer immutable group IDs) or if your system uses display names that can change? If they’re mutable, the SIG will want mapping to stable IDs.

If you can drop the extra CSV (user-attribute-cardinality.csv) by EOD tomorrow that should be enough. After that we’ll close the ticket and upload to the SIG portal.

Best,
Alice
